test: EQ004 — OU with nflfastR exponential clock kernel, k sweep
spec: mu_path(t) = close * exp(-k * t/3600); nflfastR uses k=4 (10.4min kernel half-life)
verdict: DIAGNOSTIC — the parametric kernel vs the empirical attractor: whichever wins becomes the live-WP base.
label: DIAGNOSTIC
finding: k sweep 2→8 monotone improves (0.2130→0.2095) — larger kernel decay always helps, i.e. the faster the market path dies, the better the process predicts. But ALL k lose to the empirical attractor (0.1896). The empirical curve captures shape the parametric kernel cannot (the big-favorite build-to-peak-then-ease). VERDICT: empirical attractor is the keeper; the kernel sweep confirms the DIRECTION (faster decay = better) and suggests the empirical curve should also be re-fitted with faster late-game decay.
